title: Telemetry Golden Set and Lint Runbook for SDKs
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Overview:

This runbook defines the Telemetry Golden Set (TGS) and the telemetry-lint gating process used by the Developer Experience (DevX) and Observability teams to keep SDK telemetry stable, high-fidelity, and actionable. The TGS is a curated, executable collection of canonical events and assertions that represent the minimum viable telemetry for each SDK release surface (auth, request, streaming, error, and cost). The lint rules verify schema, sampling, and cardinality constraints before merge and during canary.

Goals:
- Ensure telemetry events emitted by SDKs conform to schema and naming conventions.
- Prevent regressions that cause metric loss, alert noise, or ingestion spikes.
- Provide fast local and CI feedback with reproducible golden cases.
- Make telemetry changes discoverable, reviewed, and backwards-compatible.

Scope and ownership:
- Applies to: all official Redwood SDKs (Python, Go, Node, Java).
- Owned by: DevX Observability (primary), SDK Owners (secondary).
- CI gates enforced in: ci/telemetry-golden-check (pre-merge), ci/telemetry-canary (post-merge).

Definitions:
- Telemetry Golden Set (TGS): a suite of 12–30 canonical event payloads + assertions per SDK that exercise common and edge behavior. Each payload has a unique id in the repo under /telemetry/golden/ and a human-readable description.
- telemetry-lint: the validation tool used in local and CI pipelines to run schema checks, delta analysis, and sampling verification.

Required signals in every SDK TGS (minimum):
1) sdk.init (startup) — includes sdk.version, platform, commit_sha.
2) request.start, request.end — includes route_id, model_name, token_count_estimate.
3) stream.chunk (if streaming) — includes sequence, bytes, is_final.
4) error.report — includes error_code, retryable, stack_hash.
5) cost.estimate and cost.actual — includes token_units, batching_enabled.
6) auth.failure — includes method, status_code.

Schema & linting rules (selected):
- Event keys must be snake_case and use the approved prefix set: [sdk, request, stream, error, cost, auth].
- Required fields: event_type, timestamp_iso, sdk_version, environment, trace_id (uuid4).
- No free-text large blobs: max payload size 8KB for golden events.
- Cardinality rule: label keys limited to 20 unique values per 24h test window for golden inputs.
- Sampling assertion: sample_rate reported must match the test harness value (avoid accidental 0 or 1 flips).
- Backwards compat rule: new required fields must be feature-flagged and opt-in for two minor releases.

Sample telemetry-lint config (telemetry-lint.yaml):

code:
# telemetry-lint.yaml
version: 1
rules:
  - id: schema-required-fields
    severity: error
    required: ["event_type", "timestamp_iso", "sdk_version", "trace_id"]
  - id: snake-case-keys
    severity: error
  - id: max-payload-bytes
    severity: warning
    max_bytes: 8192
  - id: sampling-match
    severity: error
    enforce_ci: true

Local developer quickstart (run before pushing):
1) Install validator: pip install redwood-telemetry-lint (or npm i -D @redwood/telemetry-lint).
2) Build golden cases: python tools/golden/pack.py --sdk python --out .telemetry-pack.json
3) Run lint: telemetry-lint verify --config telemetry-lint.yaml .telemetry-pack.json
4) Run diff against upstream TGS to see added/removed events: telemetry-lint diff --base origin/main --head HEAD

CI pipeline behavior (ci/telemetry-golden-check):
- Trigger: PR to any SDK main branch that touches src/ or telemetry/ directories.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout and build SDK artifact.
  2. Execute telemetry-lint verify with the official config.
  3. Run golden harness to emit events to the local validator and assert: schema passes, sample_rate equal, no cardinality spikes.
  4. Produce a delta report artifact (telemetry-delta.json) and a human-readable summary posted as PR comment.
- Failure modes: schema errors -> block merge. sampling mismatches -> block merge. cardinality warnings -> require approver from observability team to override.

Canary and post-merge verification (ci/telemetry-canary):
- After merge to main, the CI job runs the TGS against the canary ingestion path for 24 hours:
  - Canary checks: ingestion latency p95 < 2s, event-drop rate < 0.1%, schema violations = 0.
  - If any canary threshold is violated, automatic rollback runbook is triggered (see Runbook: Canary failure).

Runbook: CI pre-merge failure
1) Read the telemetry-delta.json artifact attached to the PR.
2) If schema error: fix event keys/types or add compatibility wrapper (e.g., provide fallback key).
3) If sampling mismatch: ensure sample_rate is intentionally set or update harness to include new sampling behavior and explain in PR description.
4) If cardinality spike: reduce dimension cardinality in the event or add normalization.
5) Request observability review by tagging @devx-observability in PR and include impacted routes.

Runbook: Canary failure (post-merge)
1) Pager alert to #oncall-observability (severity P2) is created by canary job and includes delta report and ingest metrics.
2) Triage steps:
  a. Confirm job reproducibility with: telemetry-lint verify --canary --head main
  b. Check ingestion pipeline health: (metrics) ingest.errors.count > 0? consumer-lag > 10s?
  c. If ingestion is healthy but schema violations occur, open a rollback PR to revert SDK change and notify SDK owner.
  d. If sampling or cardinality causes cost spike, enable rate-limiting fallback in the runtime: export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLER=0.01 and roll a hotfix.
3) Postmortem within 72 hours required if canary error budget impact > 0.5% of daily events.

Change process for telemetry schema updates (recommended):
1) Create a design doc with backward compatibility plan and canary gating matrix.
2) Add new field as optional and include automated conversion shim in the SDK.
3) Update TGS with golden cases for both old and new schema.
4) Run pre-merge telemetry-lint and submit for Observability review.
5) Merge and monitor canary for 48 hours.
6) After two successful minor releases (>= 2 weeks each), promote field to required and remove shim.

Debugging recipes and tooling tips:
- Quick export for local debugging: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_DUMP=1 telemetry-lint run .telemetry-pack.json > /tmp/telemetry-dump.ndjson
- Validate a single JSON event: telemetry-lint check-event --schema schemas/sdk-event.json event.json
- Diff against production golden set snapshot: telemetry-lint snapshot-diff --prod snapshot_2027-01-10.ndjson --head .telemetry-pack.json

Ownership and contact points:
- Primary owner: DevX Observability (team alias: devx-observability@redwood.dev).
- SDK owners must maintain their SDK TGS under sdk/<language>/telemetry/golden/.
- Oncall: see team run rotations in /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations.

Metrics and SLOs used in gating decisions:
- Ingestion latency: p95 < 2s (canary), p99 < 5s (production baseline).
- Event-drop rate: < 0.1% during canary; <0.05% production.
- Schema violation rate: 0 for canary and first 24h after merge.
- Golden test coverage: >= 85% of public API surface for the SDK (measured by route/feature mapping).

Rollout checklist (pre-release):
- [ ] TGS updated and committed with descriptive changelog for each golden case.
- [ ] telemetry-lint passes locally and in ci/telemetry-golden-check.
- [ ] Observability review completed and documented in PR.
- [ ] Post-merge canary monitoring enabled and alert thresholds set.
- [ ] Documentation updated on docs-site (sdk telemetry sections) including sample events and migration notes.

Appendix: Example minimal event (sdk.request.end)
{
  "event_type": "request.end",
  "timestamp_iso": "2027-01-12T14:22:08.512Z",
  "sdk_version": "python-0.9.3",
  "trace_id": "4f3a8f30-9c7b-4f1d-9b0a-9a2e1c6b8f2e",
  "route_id": "embed-2027-01",
  "model_name": "rw-medium-v1",
  "token_count_estimate": 48,
  "token_units": 0.0032,
  "sampling_rate": 0.02
}

Notes and rationale:
- The golden set approach emphasizes reproducibility: CI and local tooling should exercise identical cases so that deltas are meaningful.
- Linting early prevents costly post-deploy rollbacks (telemetry changes are often high blast radius).
- The two-release grace period balances developer velocity and production safety for schema evolution.

Related resources and templates:
- telemetry-lint repo: git@github.com:redwood/telemetry-lint.git
- Golden pack builder: tools/golden/pack.py (see README in repo).
- PR template: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/telemetry-change.md

If you are adding or changing any telemetry event and are unsure if it belongs in the golden set, open a quick consult in #devx-telemetry with the tag [golden-consult] and include the event JSON and intended runtime frequency.
